answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period before its actions count toward reputation or rewards. A Sybil attacker can still create many identities, but must fund and immobilize a separate stake for each, so multiplying influence ties up capital and exposes it to slashing when identities coordinate to cheat. The rule acts as an anchor: saffron-tier agents might earn higher limits, while orchard-like clusters of fresh accounts remain costly to sustain.
